_comment: "Up to one target defending ACTION CARD gets +3{d} this turn." The +3 was applied to the defending TOTAL with neither the target nor max_targets read, so a block made entirely of equipment -- where the card has no legal target at all -- still got +3{d}. With a target the two agree whenever an action card is defending and part company exactly where the card is restrictive. "Up to one" is modelled as "one if there is a legal target, none otherwise" rather than as a prompt: +3{d} on a card you chose to defend with is never a downside, so declining is never correct play.
